title: Cloud Concepts, Google Cloud Infrastructure and Service Models

header.html: 1.2 Describe fundamental cloud concepts: the business use case and benefits of private cloud, hybrid cloud and multicloud; fundamental networking concepts; the components of Google Cloud's network (regions, zones, edge locations); the benefits and tradeoffs of IaaS, PaaS and SaaS
the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide

toc.title: Service models: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS

html:
1Cloud architectures

Architecture What it is Business use case
On-premises Your own data center Full control; high upfront cost, slow to scale
Public cloud Resources shared on a provider's infrastructure, paid by use Speed, scale and low startup cost
Private cloud Cloud-style resources for one organization Strict control or regulation
Hybrid cloud On-premises or private plus public cloud, connected Move step by step; keep sensitive or legacy systems on site
Multicloud More than one public cloud provider Avoid lock-in, choose the best service for each job, resilience
Exam tip

. Hybrid = on-premises plus cloud. Multicloud = more than one cloud provider. Hybrid is the answer for "keep some systems in our own data center".

2Networking basics

Term Meaning
IP address The numeric address of a device on a network
Domain name service (DNS) Turns names such as example.com into IP addresses
Latency The delay before data arrives; lower is better
Bandwidth The amount of data a connection can carry; higher is better

Latency depends on distance, so placing resources near users helps.

3Google Cloud's global infrastructure

Component Meaning
Region A geographic area with several zones
Zone A deployment area inside a region, with independent power, cooling and networking; a failure in one zone should not affect others
Edge location A network point of presence close to users that caches content and connects to Google's network
Global network Google's own fiber network, including subsea cables, that connects regions and edge locations

Multiple zones give high availability; multiple regions give disaster recovery and lower latency for global users. The network carries traffic on Google's own private backbone instead of the public internet where possible, for speed and security.

Exam tip

. Zone = failure domain inside a region. Region = geographic area. Spread across zones for availability, across regions for disaster recovery and reach.

4Service models: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS

Model You get You manage Example on Google Cloud
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) Virtual machines, storage, networks Operating system, applications, data Compute Engine
Platform as a Service (PaaS) A platform to build and run apps Applications and data Cloud Run, App Engine, BigQuery
Software as a Service (SaaS) A finished application Your data, users and settings Google Workspace, Looker
Tradeoff IaaS PaaS SaaS
Control and flexibility Highest Medium Lowest
Effort and staffing Highest Medium Lowest
Speed to value Slower Fast Fastest
Customization Most Some Least

Choose by need: maximum control → IaaS; build apps without managing servers → PaaS; a ready tool for users → SaaS.

Exam tip

. The more the provider manages, the less you control and the less you must staff. IaaS = most control, SaaS = least.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A hospital must keep patient records in its own data center but wants to use cloud analytics for other workloads. Which architecture fits?

  • APublic cloud only, with no on-premises systems left at all
  • BMulticloud only, with two public providers
  • CEdge caching only, with no data center
  • DHybrid cloud, connecting on-premises and public cloud
Show the answer

Answer: D. Hybrid cloud connects on-premises systems with public cloud services.

S2A company wants to avoid depending on one provider and chooses the best service from several public clouds. What is this?

  • AA private cloud, built for one organization
  • BA hybrid cloud, with only one public provider involved
  • CAn on-premises design, with no providers
  • DA multicloud strategy, using several providers
Show the answer

Answer: D. Using more than one public cloud provider is multicloud.

S3A single data center failure in a region must not stop an application. What is the best design?

  • ARun everything in one zone with a larger server
  • BPlace all servers at the edge locations
  • CMove the application to a private network
  • DSpread the application across several zones
Show the answer

Answer: D. Zones are independent failure domains; spreading across zones gives high availability.

S4Which term describes the delay before data arrives from a server?

  • ABandwidth, the amount a connection carries
  • BDNS, the translation of names
  • CIP address, the number of a device
  • DLatency, the delay in delivery
Show the answer

Answer: D. Latency is the delay; lower latency means faster responses.

S5A startup wants to deploy its own web application without managing servers or operating systems. Which service model fits best?

  • AIaaS, because it gives virtual machines to manage
  • BSaaS, because it is a finished application
  • CPaaS, because it provides a platform to run apps
  • DOn-premises, because it gives full control
Show the answer

Answer: C. Platform as a Service lets a team run its own code without managing the underlying servers.

S6A company needs full control of the operating system and installed software on its servers in the cloud. Which model fits?

  • ASaaS, with the lowest management effort
  • BPaaS, with a managed application platform
  • CIaaS, with virtual machines it manages
  • DA fully managed analytics warehouse
Show the answer

Answer: C. IaaS gives the most control, and the customer manages the operating system and above.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is hybrid cloud?

Show the answer

On-premises or private resources connected with public cloud.

R2What is multicloud?

Show the answer

Using more than one public cloud provider.

R3What is a zone?

Show the answer

A deployment area inside a region with independent infrastructure.

R4What does DNS do?

Show the answer

Turns names into IP addresses.

R5Which model gives the most control?

Show the answer

IaaS.

R6Is Compute Engine IaaS or PaaS?

Show the answer

IaaS.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Architectures on-premises, public, private, hybrid (on-premises plus cloud), multicloud (several clouds)
Network IP, DNS, latency (delay), bandwidth (capacity)
Google Cloud network regions, zones (failure domains), edge locations, global fiber network
Service models IaaS most control, PaaS apps and data, SaaS least effort
